title: Magnetism: fields, quantum matter and controlled inference
summary: A source-linked hierarchy from classical currents and magnetic energy to quantum materials, spin transport, superconducting screening and reproducible magnetometry.
scope: Selected foundations and2024–2026 primary/preprint evidence. Not an exhaustive literature survey, patentability opinion, material certification or hardware demonstration. Abstract-only papers and unreviewed branches remain explicitly marked.

formulas.title: Magnetic flux continuity
formulas.plain: Divergence-free B has zero net outward flux through a closed surface.
conditions: Classical Maxwell theory with no magnetic monopoles; include all faces of a closed surface.
derivation: Apply the divergence theorem to local flux continuity.
Opposite face contributions cancel for a uniform field.

workedExample.inputs: Bz=0.01 T; cube side=0.1 m
steps: Top flux=+0.0001 Wb; bottom=-0.0001 Wb; sides zero.

limitingCases: A nonzero open-surface flux is entirely compatible.
pitfalls: Zero divergence does not imply zero curl or zero local field.

formulas.title: Biot–Savart law for a filament
formulas.latex: \mathbf B(\mathbf r)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int \frac{d\boldsymbol\ell\times(\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime)}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime|^3}
formulas.plain: Sum oriented steady-current elements using the inverse-distance vector kernel.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
oriented line element in current direction

conditions: Steady localized current with a physically completed return path; vacuum.
Observation point is outside the ideal filament.
derivation: Solve the vector Poisson equation in Coulomb gauge with the free-space Green function.
Take its curl to obtain the cross-product kernel.

workedExample.inputs: Circular loop I=1 A, R=0.1 m; evaluate centre
steps: All axial contributions add; transverse contributions cancel.
Integrate circumference to obtain mu0 I/(2R).

limitingCases: The far field of a localized closed loop is dipolar, not an isolated-wire 1/r field.
pitfalls: Do not omit return current when predicting a finite device field.

formulas.title: Infinite straight wire
formulas.plain: Cylindrical symmetry turns Ampere circulation into an azimuthal field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Infinite thin wire, vacuum, stationary current; r exceeds conductor radius.
derivation: Choose a coaxial circular contour.
B is tangential and constant on the contour, so 2 pi r B=mu0 I.
limitingCases: As I tends to zero, B vanishes; the singular r→0 limit is outside the thin-wire domain.
pitfalls: A finite wire cannot inherit this expression arbitrarily close to its ends.

formulas.title: On-axis circular-loop field
formulas.plain: The axial field of a thin circular loop interpolates between centre field and a dipole.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Circular filament in vacuum; observation on its symmetry axis.
derivation: Project the Biot–Savart cross product onto the axis.
The denominator is constant around the loop; integrate azimuth.
limitingCases: At z=0 recover mu0 I/(2R); for |z|≫R recover z^-3.
pitfalls: The expression is not the off-axis field of a finite solenoid.

formulas.title: Magnetostatic free-current circulation
formulas.plain: H circulation counts free current after magnetization is separated out.
conditions: Stationary fields; displacement current negligible; contour and normal follow right-hand orientation.
derivation: Apply Stokes theorem to curl H=Jf.
Integrate current density over the spanning surface.

workedExample.inputs: Ienc=3 A; circular contour radius=0.1 m with cylindrical symmetry

limitingCases: Zero enclosed current gives zero circulation, not necessarily H=0 everywhere.
pitfalls: Ampere law does not justify constant H on a nonsymmetric contour.

formulas.title: Long-solenoid interior estimate
formulas.plain: Turns per unit length set the ideal long air-core coil field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Length much larger than radius, observation away from ends, air core, negligible winding thickness.
derivation: Choose an Ampere rectangle along the interior and remote exterior.
Neglect exterior contribution and count n*l turns.
limitingCases: At an ideal long coil end the on-axis field is about half the deep-interior value.
pitfalls: Real coil heating, fringe fields and magnetic core saturation are separate calculations.

formulas.title: Macroscopic B–H–M relation
formulas.plain: Magnetization is magnetic moment per material volume; the relation defines H in SI.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Macroscopic SI fields defined at compatible coarse-graining scale.
derivation: Separate microscopic current into free and magnetization contributions.
Define H=B/mu0−M; no linear material law is assumed.

workedExample.inputs: Collinear H=100 A/m and M=900 A/m

limitingCases: For M=0, vacuum B=mu0 H; at H=0 an ordered sample can have M≠0.
pitfalls: B and H do not have the same SI units; B=mu H additionally assumes a constitutive law.

formulas.title: Volume magnetization current
formulas.plain: Spatially varying magnetization has an equivalent bound volume current.
conditions: Continuum magnetization differentiable inside the material; add interface surface currents separately.
derivation: Represent localized magnetic moments as small current loops.
Interior loop contributions cancel except where magnetization varies.
limitingCases: Uniform M has zero volume curl but generally nonzero surface current.
pitfalls: Zero Jb in the bulk does not imply an unmagnetized body.

formulas.title: Surface magnetization current
formulas.plain: The boundary current closes magnetization loops at an interface.
conditions: Use the magnetization jump if both sides are magnetic; orientation is outward from the chosen body.
derivation: Integrate volume curl through an infinitesimal interface layer.
The normal derivative of the magnetization step produces a surface sheet.

workedExample.inputs: M=1000 zhat A/m; surface normal=xhat

limitingCases: A face normal parallel to M carries no equivalent surface current.
pitfalls: The order M cross n matters; reversing it reverses circulation.

formulas.title: Far-field magnetic dipole
formulas.latex: \mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r^3}[3(\mathbf m\cdot\hat{\mathbf r})\hat{\mathbf r}-\mathbf m]
formulas.plain: A localized current distribution has a leading magnetic dipole term.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: r much larger than source extent; outside the source in vacuum.
derivation: Expand the localized vector potential at large distance.
The closed-current monopole term vanishes; curl the leading moment term.

workedExample.inputs: m=0.1 A m²; axial r=0.1 m

limitingCases: At the equator the field points opposite m with half the axial magnitude.
pitfalls: The singular point-dipole field cannot describe the source interior.

formulas.title: Dipole torque and energy
formulas.plain: A fixed permanent dipole tends to align with the applied field.
conditions: Small fixed moment in a field uniform over the dipole; induced moments require material work accounting.
derivation: Sum Lorentz forces around a small loop.
Integrate torque against angle to obtain U=−mB cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: m=0.01 A m²; B=0.1 T; perpendicular orientation
workedExample.result: Torque=0.001 N m; aligned U=−0.001 J

limitingCases: Aligned torque is zero although energy is minimal, not zero by necessity.
pitfalls: An induced moment may introduce a factor1/2 in energy after its formation is included.

formulas.title: Force on a fixed dipole
formulas.plain: The gradient of dipole potential gives force when its moment is fixed.
conditions: Small rigid moment, quasistatic external field, derivatives at fixed m.
derivation: Use F=−gradient U with U=−m dot B.
Keep self field and induced-response work outside this simplified potential.

workedExample.inputs: mz=0.01 A m²; dBz/dz=2 T/m
steps: Multiply mz by axial field gradient.

limitingCases: A uniform field can exert torque but gives no translational dipole force.
pitfalls: A field magnitude alone is insufficient to determine lifting force.

formulas.title: Magnetic flux
formulas.plain: Flux is the oriented surface integral, not B multiplied by any convenient area.

variables.meaning: magnetic flux through chosen oriented surface

conditions: A defined surface and normal; B and geometry may vary across it.
derivation: Sum infinitesimal normal field contributions.
For a uniform field and flat area, obtain BA cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: B=0.2 T; A=0.01 m²; field at60degrees to normal

limitingCases: A surface parallel to field has zero flux despite nonzero B.
pitfalls: Angle is measured from the normal, not from the surface plane.

formulas.title: Oriented moving-loop Faraday law
formulas.plain: Electric and motional contributions give the emf around the actual moving material loop.
conditions: A well-defined material circuit and right-hand orientation; ideal thin circuit approximation.
derivation: Combine local curl E=−partial B/partial t with the moving-surface transport theorem.
The boundary motion term is v cross B, not an extra energy source.

workedExample.inputs: Stationary loop, flux rises by0.003 Wb over0.1 s
workedExample.result: emf=−0.03 V for the chosen positive circulation

limitingCases: Steady B can induce emf if the loop area/orientation changes.
pitfalls: Reversing the chosen normal reverses both flux and emf sign consistently.

formulas.title: Ampère–Maxwell law
formulas.plain: Free current and displacement-current density both source the curl of H.
conditions: Macroscopic Maxwell equations with polarization placed in D.
derivation: Add displacement current to preserve free-charge continuity.
Taking divergence gives divergence Jf+partial rho_f/partial t=0 using divergence D=rho_f.

workedExample.inputs: Charging capacitor: dD/dt=2 A/m² over0.01 m²
steps: Integrate displacement current density over gap area.

limitingCases: The term may be negligible in a specific MQS limit, not identically absent.
pitfalls: Displacement current is not a flow of free charges across an ideal vacuum capacitor gap.

formulas.title: Vacuum Poynting theorem
formulas.latex: \partial_t u+\nabla\cdot\mathbf S=-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf E,\quad\mathbf S=\mathbf E\times\mathbf H
formulas.plain: Field storage plus outward electromagnetic flux equals negative work rate on matter.
conditions: Vacuum fields with material currents treated explicitly; material storage needs a consistent constitutive energy model.
derivation: Dot Ampère–Maxwell with E and Faraday with H.
Subtract using divergence(E cross H)=H dot curl E−E dot curl H.

workedExample.inputs: Control volume: inward flux3 W; stored-energy rise1 W
steps: Outward integrated S=−3 W; dU/dt=1 W.

limitingCases: A steady state can have nonzero energy flux while storage is constant.
pitfalls: Field enhancement is not net output; include every boundary port and initial storage.

formulas.title: Vacuum field-energy density
formulas.plain: Quadratic vacuum storage follows from reversible field work.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Vacuum or a specified linear nondispersive analogue; not a general hysteretic-material formula.
derivation: Integrate E dD and H dB along a reversible constitutive path.
In vacuum D=epsilon0 E and H=B/mu0.

workedExample.inputs: E=0; B=0.01 T in volume0.001 m³

limitingCases: Storage vanishes quadratically as B→0.
pitfalls: Using B²/(2mu) in a nonlinear hysteretic core can give incorrect material energy accounting.

formulas.title: Passive inductor and winding budget
formulas.plain: Source power splits into changing magnetic storage and nonnegative winding dissipation.
conditions: L positive and constant, R≥0, no additional coupled or powered ports.
derivation: Multiply voltage equation by current.
Use L i di/dt=d(Li²/2)/dt.

workedExample.inputs: L=0.1 H; i rises0→2 A; R=0 for illustrative storage
workedExample.result: Input work=0.2 J; no continuous output from a fixed stored state

limitingCases: With source off, a resistor can drain initial energy but cannot replenish it.
pitfalls: A changing L introduces mechanical/coupling work; do not omit it.

formulas.title: Cycle work in magnetic material
formulas.plain: An oriented quasistatic B–H loop gives magnetic work per sample volume for a completed cycle.

variables.meaning: net supplied work per cycle per volume

conditions: Closed periodic cycle, consistent internal field and sample volume; separate nonmagnetic apparatus losses.
derivation: Integrate local magnetic work H dot dB.
Reversible storage returns to its initial value after a cycle, leaving net dissipative work.

workedExample.inputs: Rectangular scalar loop: coercive Hc=100 A/m; remanent Br=0.5 T
workedExample.result: Dissipated work=200 J/m³ per cycle under this loop idealization

limitingCases: A reversible single-valued path traversed forward and back encloses zero area.
pitfalls: A counterclockwise plotted loop may change algebraic sign; passivity uses work supplied to matter.

formulas.title: Ellipsoidal internal-field correction
formulas.plain: A uniform ellipsoid gives a closed correction for reversible scalar susceptibility.
conditions: Uniform ellipsoid, principal-axis drive, linear reversible medium; SI factors sum to1.
derivation: Combine demagnetizing field −NM with M=chi Hint.
Solve the one-variable linear equation for M.

workedExample.inputs: Sphere N=1/3; chi=3; Happ=100 A/m

limitingCases: For chi→0, M≈chi Happ; large chi is shape-limited.
pitfalls: CGS demagnetizing factors can sum to4pi; do not mix conventions.

formulas.title: Weak-field Curie susceptibility
formulas.plain: Independent isotropically orientable moments respond linearly when thermal energy dominates alignment.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Noninteracting moments in weak field mu B≪kB T; classical orientation or appropriate quantum effective moment.
derivation: For classical isotropic independent moments use x=mu B/(kB T) and Z_orientation=4pi sinh(x)/x. Its mean axial moment is mu[coth(x)−1/x].
Expand coth(x)−1/x=x/3+O(x³), multiply by number density, and use B≈mu0 H in this weak-response limit. This is an explanatory derivation, distinct from the source’s two-state Ising normalization.
limitingCases: The expression cannot be extrapolated to T=0 or saturation.
pitfalls: It is not a ferromagnetic hysteresis law and does not include exchange correlations.
An Ising two-state moment has a different weak-field angular factor; do not import its normalized B coupling as SI tesla.

formulas.title: Curie–Weiss phenomenology
formulas.plain: A molecular-field correction shifts the Curie-law denominator.
conditions: Paramagnetic regime sufficiently far from transitions; fitted C and theta are model-dependent.
derivation: Assume an effective field H+lambda M and insert the Curie response.
Solve for M/H and absorb molecular-field coefficient into theta.

workedExample.inputs: C=0.1 K; T=300 K; theta=50 K

limitingCases: theta=0 recovers Curie behavior; the denominator divergence is not a literal finite-sample infinity.
pitfalls: Negative theta suggests dominant AFM correlations, not proof of a spin liquid or an ordering temperature.

formulas.title: Heisenberg exchange convention
formulas.plain: With this plus-sign convention, positive J favors antiparallel spin correlations.

variables.meaning: dimensionless spin operator at site i

conditions: Specify lattice, spin magnitude, boundary and omitted anisotropy/dipolar terms.
derivation: Reduce an electronic low-energy problem to spin degrees of freedom under declared assumptions.
For two spin1/2 particles, S1 dot S2 has eigenvalues−3/4 and+1/4.

workedExample.inputs: One bond J=1 meV

limitingCases: For J<0 the triplet is lower in this convention.
pitfalls: Some authors write−J S dot S and reverse the meaning of positive J.

formulas.title: Classical triangular AFM counterexample
formulas.latex: E=J(\mathbf s_1\cdot\mathbf s_2+\mathbf s_2\cdot\mathbf s_3+\mathbf s_3\cdot\mathbf s_1)
formulas.plain: Three unit spins cannot make all three AFM bonds antiparallel.
conditions: Classical isotropic spins on a single triangular plaquette, zero field.
derivation: Write E=J(|s1+s2+s3|²−3)/2.
The lower bound occurs when the three vectors sum to zero.

workedExample.inputs: J=1 energy unit; coplanar angles0,120,240degrees
workedExample.result: Emin=−1.5 J rather than the impossible−3 J

limitingCases: The 120degree classical ground state is ordered; frustration alone is not a quantum-spin-liquid proof.
pitfalls: Do not transfer a three-site classical minimum to an infinite quantum lattice without analysis.

formulas.title: Gilbert dynamics with positive gamma convention
formulas.latex: \dot{\mathbf m}=-\frac{\gamma}{1+\alpha^2}[\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff}+\alpha\mathbf m\times(\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff})]
formulas.plain: A unit magnetization precesses and damps with a declared positive gyromagnetic magnitude.

variables.meaning: effective induction including selected energy terms

conditions: Fixed saturation magnitude; differentiable effective energy; torque sources and temperature terms must be added explicitly.
derivation: Solve Gilbert implicit equation dm/dt=−gamma m cross B+alpha m cross dm/dt.
Use m dot dm/dt=0 to invert its tangent-plane operator.

workedExample.inputs: alpha=0; Bz=0.1 T; gamma=1.760e11 rad/(T s)
steps: Angular rate=gamma B=1.760e10 rad/s; divide by2pi.

limitingCases: With alpha=0 and static energy, precession conserves energy; alpha>0 removes energy for the consistent convention.
pitfalls: The selected MuMax paper prints a plus-prefactor gamma_LL form; this entry chooses positive gamma and an explicit minus sign. Check the source convention and actual precession direction before converting symbols.

formulas.title: Continuum exchange energy and effective field
formulas.plain: A smooth magnetization texture costs gradient energy and creates a restoring exchange field.
conditions: Constant A and Ms; slowly varying texture; appropriate fixed or natural boundaries.
derivation: Vary the gradient functional and integrate by parts.
Use Beff=−(1/Ms) deltaE/deltam as a volume functional derivative.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; sinusoidal wave k=1e7/m; Ms=8e5 A/m

limitingCases: Uniform m has zero exchange energy in this reference.
pitfalls: A mesh that cannot resolve rotation between cells misrepresents this continuum model.

formulas.title: Uniaxial anisotropy convention
formulas.plain: Positive K in this convention favors alignment along either easy-axis direction.
conditions: One uniaxial contribution with a chosen zero of energy; other anisotropies may coexist.
derivation: Expand a time-reversal-even scalar energy in the axis projection.
Subtract a constant so aligned states have zero energy.

workedExample.inputs: K=1e5 J/m³; m at45degrees to u

limitingCases: Parallel and antiparallel easy-axis states are degenerate under this term alone.
pitfalls: A negative coefficient changes the easy directions; do not infer them from the symbol K alone.

formulas.title: Interfacial DMI energy convention
formulas.plain: An inversion-asymmetric interfacial invariant favors one texture chirality.

variables.meaning: DMI energy per volume in effective thin-film convention

workedExample.inputs: A=1.3e-11 J/m; Ms=8e5 A/m

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; K=1e5 J/m³

effective magnetization including declared perpendicular anisotropy

conditions: Small-amplitude mode, uniform equilibrium, neglect dipolar dispersion/anisotropy or absorb appropriate constants in B0.

Linearize undamped LLG to get precession with the shifted restoring field.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; Ms=8e5 A/m; k=1e7/m; gamma/(2pi)=28 GHz/T

limitingCases: As k→0 the exchange shift vanishes, but other gap terms may remain.

formulas.title: Skyrmion degree

conditions: Fixed common boundary direction or compact domain; no singular point where |m| vanishes.
derivation: Integrate oriented area swept on the unit sphere and normalize by4pi.

workedExample.inputs: Azimuthal winding n=1; core theta=pi; boundary theta=0
workedExample.result: Q=−1; reversing orientation conventions can reverse its sign

limitingCases: A uniform state has Q=0; a boundary-unfixed partial texture need not give an integer.
pitfalls: Topological charge alone does not guarantee infinite lifetime or free energy; boundaries and singular events permit changes.

formulas.title: Spin Hall normalization
formulas.plain: A declared scalar spin Hall angle relates selected spin-angular-momentum flux to charge current density.

variables.meaning: signed conversion angle for stated axes

conditions: A specified material, transport geometry and spin polarization convention; tensor character suppressed only for one chosen component.
For this scalar example define charge along+x, flux along+z and polarization along+y; the signed thetaSH is defined for exactly that ordered axis choice.
derivation: Express spin flux as angular momentum per transported carrier.
Define thetaSH by the ratio of normalized transverse spin flux to charge flux.

workedExample.inputs: thetaSH=0.1; jc=1e10 A/m²
workedExample.result: js=3.29106e-7 J/m² in the angular-momentum-flux convention

limitingCases: Changing spin-flux convention to charge-equivalent A/m² removes the hbar/(2e) prefactor.
pitfalls: A spin current is not an extra source of energy; injector electrical power and interface losses remain.

conditions: A selected torque term in an explicitly powered model; two-sublattice AFMs require the corresponding sublattice torques.

formulas.title: London penetration in a half-space

conditions: Static homogeneous London regime, planar surface, weak fields without vortices or strong nonlocality; bulk boundary B→0.

Select the decaying solution of the one-dimensional second-order equation.

workedExample.inputs: B(0)=1 mT; lambdaL=100 nm; z=200 nm

limitingCases: The growing exponential is excluded by the bulk boundary condition.
pitfalls: An ideal perfect conductor preserves initial flux; equilibrium Meissner expulsion needs more than infinite DC conductivity.

formulas.title: Superconducting flux quantum and fluxoid
formulas.plain: Single-valued pair phase quantizes a fluxoid, with magnetic flux alone recovered when the current term is negligible.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Closed contour in a coherent superconducting region; conventional2e pairing assumed; finite kinetic-current correction retained.

workedExample.inputs: h=6.62607015e-34 J s; e=1.602176634e-19 C; n=1; negligible current correction

limitingCases: In thin/high-kinetic-inductance loops, flux need not equal nPhi0 even though fluxoid does.

conditions: Conventional isotropic GL description near its controlled transition regime; orbital limit, neglect paramagnetic/multiband modifications.

glossary.definition: B is magnetic induction in tesla; H is field intensity in ampere per metre. B=mu0(H+M) does not by itself assume a linear material.
International System of Units. The revised SI fixes h and e, while mu0 is experimentally inferred.
Ferromagnetic / antiferromagnetic / unequal opposing sublattice order; net moment alone does not specify a magnetic phase.
An antiferromagnetic sublattice-difference order parameter; its normalization must be declared.
Magnetoquasistatic approximation: retain induction while neglecting displacement current only under an appropriate scale analysis.
Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, an antisymmetric exchange contribution allowed by appropriate inversion-symmetry breaking.
Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert dynamics. Signed gyromagnetic conventions and B-versus-H choices must remain consistent.
Spin–orbit torque / spin-transfer torque. Both require an angular-momentum source and a complete electrical/thermal budget.
Density functional theory and increasingly structured exchange-correlation approximations; Hubbard U is an additional model parameter, not an automatic measured constant.
Nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond; an orientation-dependent spin sensor with its own Hamiltonian, calibration and bandwidth.
Quantum spin liquid: a proposed quantum phase requiring positive diagnostic evidence, not simply lack of observed order.
A long-period interference/registry pattern from lattice mismatch or twist; magnetic exchange depends on the actual relaxed structure.
Combined spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetry; neither a generic claim of magnetic absence nor a universal spin-degeneracy rule without the full symmetry setting.
A spin-wave excitation. A mode frequency, a driven resonance peak and a sensor spectral peak are different quantities.
Ginzburg–Landau coarse-grained order-parameter theory, especially controlled near a transition under its assumptions.
A system cannot deliver more energy than supplied plus initially stored energy over its stated ports and time window.
Verification checks implementation against a mathematical model; validation tests whether that model predicts the measured physical system.
Abstract-only, selected text and metadata identify different evidence levels; a source hash proves identity, not truth.
A statistical standard uncertainty, a deterministic numerical error bound and an assumed manufacturing tolerance are distinct.
Different contributions to angular-momentum transport can produce similar electrical/THz signals; a channel model is required.
Magnetic flux plus a supercurrent term; it is not always identical to magnetic flux through a loop.

openQuestions.question: When can a magnetic field map uniquely identify a vector magnetization?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Provide an injective forward map under explicit support, boundary and prior constraints; report rank/null-space witnesses and held-out multi-height/multi-axis data.

openQuestions.question: Which RuO2 specimens actually support a magnetic ordered state and which conversion channel is measured?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Independent order-sensitive measurements on the same structurally characterized specimen; separate spin/orbital injection and interface response.

openQuestions.question: Which kagome plateau ansatz survives thermodynamic and independent-method comparison?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Matched Hamiltonian/boundaries, larger-size convergence, unbiased observable comparisons and independent algorithms.

openQuestions.question: How robust is phase coexistence to twist relaxation, defects and sensor transfer functions?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Correlated structural and vector-magnetic imaging with independently calibrated temperature and height.

openQuestions.question: Does the recent graphene observation uniquely identify a magnetic pairing mechanism?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Independent phase-sensitive and spin/valley-resolved constraints plus competing-phonon/electrostatic models.

openQuestions.question: What is the complete switching energy and error rate of an ultrafast torque device?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Calibrated delivered pulse work, heat, retention, write/read error distributions and auxiliary electronics accounting.

openQuestions.question: What departures from local London screening distinguish geometry from unconventional physics?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Known sample geometry, vortex history, penetration/coherence lengths and independent field calibration.
